## Course Overview {.section-card}

Welcome to **{{< var course.number >}}** — {{< var course.term >}}.

This course covers the **end-to-end data science workflow** — from setting up your Python environment and mastering the terminal, through data wrangling with NumPy and Pandas, to packaging your code and building interactive dashboards.

## Course Goals

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

- Understand the **end-to-end data science workflow**, from project setup to deployment
- Apply **core Python libraries** (NumPy, Pandas) for data manipulation and analysis
- Evaluate **data quality** — handling missing values, joins, and data import challenges
- Communicate **results through reproducible reports and interactive dashboards**

## What You'll Do Each Week

- **Before class:** Review the week's slides and any assigned readings
- **In class:** Attend lecture, participate in the code demo
- **After class:** Complete the assigned homework or project work

Slides and demos are posted on the course website and updated regularly.

## How Slides and Demos Are Organized

- Each week has its own slide deck (`slides/week-NN.qmd`)
- Each week has a companion code demo (`demos/week-NN.qmd`)
- The course website links slides and demos together
- Demos include standalone source files you can download and run

## A Quick Code Example {.demo-slide}

```python
import random

# Simulate rolling a die 10 times
rolls = [random.randint(1, 6) for _ in range(10)]
print(f"Rolls: {rolls}")
print(f"Average: {sum(rolls) / len(rolls):.2f}")
```

::: {.demo-box}
Try changing the number of rolls. Does the average get closer to 3.5?
:::
